study type: Cohort study (with cross-sectional measurements at age 21)
outcome: Brachial and aortic systolic blood pressure
Posture-related changes in systemic vascular resistance
cohort: The study included 251 women and 168 men, with a mean age of 21 years, from rural Malawi, who had been followed up since their birth.
finding: In young Malawian adults, men exhibited higher systolic blood pressure, systemic vascular resistance, and upright cardiac workload, while women showed greater posture-related changes in systemic vascular resistance and cardiac output.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken when participants were 21 years old.
